record.paper_title: Geometric curvature energies: facts, trends, and open problems
record.context_brief: Existence and stability of nonminimal critical points
record.original_question: Beyond the known global minimizers, do geometric curvature energies admit other critical points in each prescribed knot class? In particular, are there critical unknots distinct from the round circle, how many such critical configurations can occur, can critical points for different geometric curvature energies be related to one another for example by Γ-convergence, what can be proved about their stability, and can critical configurations be found in higher dimensions?

evidence.quote: Existence of critical points. For all geometric curvature energies above scale-invariance one can find (at least one) minimising knot in a given isotopy class.

Open questions 2.2.11. Are there critical points for geometric curvature energies in every prescribed knot class other than the known global minimisers? In particular, are there critical unknots different from the round circle? And if so, how many are there? Can we relate critical points of different geometric curvature energies with each other, e.g., via Γ-convergence? What can be said about the stability of such critical points? Is it possible to find critical configurations in higher dimensions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let K be a knot class, i.e., an isotopy class of smooth embeddings γ : S^1 → ℝ^3. A "geometric curvature energy" is a functional E on simple closed curves built from purely metric/geometric quantities that controls embeddedness and is scale invariant or supercritical with respect to scaling; representative examples include the Möbius energy

  E_M(γ) = ∬_{S^1×S^1} ( 1/|γ(s)-γ(t)|^2 − 1/d_γ(s,t)^2 ) |γ'(s)||γ'(t)| ds dt,

where d_γ denotes intrinsic arclength distance, the O'Hara energies E^{(α,p)}, the integral Menger curvature

  M_p(γ) = ∭ (1/R(γ(s),γ(t),γ(u)))^p ds dt du,

with R the circumradius of the three points, and the tangent-point energies TP^{(q,p)}. For each such energy E it is known that in every tame isotopy class there exists at least one minimizer.

Address the following questions:

(a) Existence of nonminimal critical points. For each of the above energies E, does every prescribed knot class contain a critical point of E (a curve γ with δE(γ)·h = 0 for every admissible variation h) that is not a global minimizer in that class?

(b) Critical unknots. Are there critical points of E in the isotopy class of the unknot which are not congruent to the round circle? If so, classify them, in particular determine how many congruence classes of such critical configurations occur.

(c) Comparison across energies. Can critical points of different geometric curvature energies be put in correspondence with one another, for instance via Γ-convergence of a suitable family of energies E_ε → E_0?

(d) Stability. Characterize the stability (positivity of the second variation, Morse index, dynamical stability under the L^2- or H^{s}-gradient flow) of the critical configurations produced in (a)–(b).

(e) Higher dimensions. For the corresponding geometric curvature energies defined on embedded closed m-dimensional submanifolds of ℝ^n (e.g., higher-dimensional tangent-point or Menger-type energies), do nonminimal critical configurations exist within prescribed isotopy classes?
artifact.status_search_result: Some sub-questions have seen partial progress: recent work (Blatt–Gilsbach–Reiter–von der Mosel) claims existence of multiple critical points for each torus knot type for the Möbius energy, and several examples of links with distinct local minima are known. However, the unknot case (whether there are critical Möbius/O'Hara unknots other than the round circle), the relations via Γ-convergence between critical sets of different energies, sharp stability results, and the higher-dimensional analogues remain largely open.

status_evidence.title: Möbius Energy of Knots and Unknots (Freedman–He–Wang)
status_evidence.snippet: Every unknot can be transformed to the round circle decreasing the Möbius energy; the round circle is the unique minimizer among unknots.
status_evidence.claim: For the Möbius energy, the round circle is the unique minimizer in the unknot class, but the existence of other critical unknots is not addressed and remains a separate question.

status_evidence.title: Discrete knot energies (arXiv:1603.02464)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of critical points and approximation/Γ-convergence results for discrete versions of knot energies.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist comparing critical points of different (discrete) geometric curvature energies via Γ-convergence-type arguments.

status_evidence.title: Knots Minimizing a Möbius-Invariant Energy (Sullivan et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical experiments show certain links possess several distinct local minima at different energy values.
status_evidence.claim: Nonminimal critical points are known to exist for some link classes; the systematic existence question for all knot classes remains open.
